notes.content: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/208b1e766e721eb32d3c2f507b21210316eb9c83.png"][/img][/p][p]Both Hangout Four and Hangout Five have been released, which means that the Hangouts feature is now finished. Please note that the price of the game will increase soon now that the Hangouts are released, so now is a good time to get the game at a reduced price![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/feabae910ff0d41f70800894d9d4cb323411111f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/cee83740cdf2b7588d988954fcd9913c81d161c7.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]With these Hangouts comes two new Outfit sets — Pirates and Suits. Whether you prefer to plunder other detective team's ships or make sure Team Tads looks spiffy for a night out on the town, you will now have the option![/p][h1]Changes to Hangouts System[/h1][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/a46d0d3ebe8eb51f06f7dcf621f05c45ff27f935.png"][/img][/p][list][*][p]Vote choices no longer impact Morale[/p][/*][*][p]Outfits now unlock when you get a good ending instead of requiring both good and bad endings[/p][/*][/list][p]The votes in each File used to impact Hangout Morale — for example, the character who you voted for as "Most Useless" would have a lower Morale when you began the Hangout. This wasn't very intuitive or clearly communicated, and led to some edge cases of players not being able to improve Morale for a character, so this is no longer the case.[/p][p]I also realized that making you play through both "good" and "bad" routes to unlock the Outfits was a little too demanding. I designed it that way so you would be encouraged to see as much of the dialog as possible, since there is some interesting dialog hidden behind "bad" options. However, asking players to try to get the characters to dislike them on purpose seemed a bit odd and confusing, especially since whether the characters like each other or not doesn't affect the dialog in the main story. After running a poll to get a sense of what solution would be best, I've now changed it so they unlock after getting good endings.[/p][p][/p][h1]Other Improvements[/h1][list][*][p]Bagels and Baguettes has been given a quieter remix to play during Hangout Two[/p][/*][*][p]Improperly aligned text in Support minigame in File 04 fixed[/p][/*][*][p]Line added for context during File 04 theories[/p][/*][*][p][/p][/*][/list][h1]File 06 Enters Production[/h1][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/57bc92553555e8598a24576d3da82998cbe6159a.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]I've started working on File 06, and judging from how long the other Files took, it will take at least six months to finish. When I release it, Methods: The Canada Files will finally be complete. It's been a longer development journey than I predicted, so thank you for your patience and for supporting the game in Early Access.[/p][p]Have fun with the new Hangouts and outfits![/p][p][/p][p]Until next time![/p][p][/p][p]— LockedOn & Erabit[/p]

notes.title: Devlog 58: How I Did It
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/6fa134d64e6d2b5e34bc6306ea1fecd3da332a0e.png[/img]

File 05 is already completed and we're finishing up translation! But how did I get it done so quickly??

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/fd0dabcb3cc9696cb96da3cd94ee17de4d41091c.png[/img]

During File 04's development, I was secretly developing File 05 simultaneously! Every time I reached a milestone, it was actually a milestone for both Files. After outlining File 04, I outlined File 05. After writing File 04, I wrote File 05. After making the sprites for File 04, I made them for File 05. Etc. At each step, I doubled my workload. 

I wasn't sure this plan would be possible to pull off, so I kept it a secret. The most essential step was to finish writing both Files — I knew that if I could do that, I could probably complete both at once. I wrote both Files across several very intense writing sessions in the span of a month— it was pretty exhausting, but definitely worth it, as I'd already reduced the amount of time that step usually takes me. Making these two Files together took nine months, instead of the usual six. So this plan of mine ended up reducing the overall development time by approximately three months. 

After File 03, I knew that the game was taking much too long to make, and the amount still left to do was daunting. After all, I'd only finished three files out of six so I still had 50% of the game left to make. I couldn't cut back on scope, so I looked at other ways I could speed things up.

One big problem I've noticed is that after releasing a File, I usually need time to recharge, but I also need to dive into writing a Hangout — this makes me a bit burned out and I was requiring more and more time to recharge between File releases.

I also realized that the Hangouts had become unwieldy — they were meant to be fun optional content, but they were taking more and more development time away from the main story.

That is why I decided to try out this idea — by developing them simultaneously, these two Files would feel like developing one File — combining the recharge time for both. And I would save writing Hangout Four until later — avoiding the dip in productivity that usually comes when I have to make the Hangouts.

In the end, this plan was successful. Which begs the question — could I have been doing it this way the whole time? It's hard to say, but I don't think so. The first three Files really required my full attention to get the formula for the game down and understand the characters I was writing. If I'd tried to rush through it, I'm convinced the quality wouldn't have held up. File 05 is a smaller scale File in many ways — an easier mystery, more indoor locations, and less new assets to create. So it was well suited to piggyback off the development of another File. Also, for the first half of development, my top priority was to get the Files out as fast as I could, as soon as I finished them. By File 03, it was obvious that my current development speed was already making the wait long — so I decided to risk making the wait between Files a little longer, if it could reduce the overall time.

Now, maybe you're wondering "Is he also secretly developing [i]Motives[/i]?" — No, unfortunately — [i]Motives[/i] has still not entered production, however I am taking some lessons from this as way to try to speed up development on [i]Motives[/i] as well. My most important takeaway from this has been that yes, I can take on more work than I previously thought at each step of the process without it affecting the quality too much. Though it does increase time between releases, that may be worth it in order to reduce the overall development time.

I hope you look forward to File 05's release. 

Until next time!

— LockedOn.

notes.title: Devlog 54: Mental Block
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/a13e4fdd2be904547557a6be942f3a6ec0692ac0.png[/img]

A devlog is definitely overdue, so here's the latest news!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/810a95a5ac55a1149841c83bb3566901167714df.png[/img]

Here's what I worked on since the last devlog!
[list]
[*] 
[*] Composing music tracks
[*] Creating 3D character models for use in CGs
[*] Drawing CGs
[*] Creating new UI elements
[*] Testing the game
[*] Implementing expressions
[*] Revising the mystery
[/list]

It's almost been two months since my last devlog — mostly because I've still not finished what I set as my next "main goal" for File 04: completing all the music.

I had the first playthroughs for File 04 in early December, and though they were very helpful, some pretty big revisions are needed. Having to go back and redo earlier work is always a huge mental block for me — it's very hard to be motivated about it. The task of composing new music combined with having to do these revisions was too much on my plate at once— I had some decision paralysis and got overwhelmed.

So instead, I worked on other things— like CGs. I'm still not done with the music or the revisions, but this month I finally was able to start working on them. The key to overcoming the mental block was to allow myself to take a bit more time on it than I thought I needed. I often underestimate the amount of time things take for me to do, because sometimes I work very quickly. However, I should not expect things to go fast while I'm doing difficult tasks, and I shouldn't put myself in a position where I have two major goals at once—it just leads to confusion. In the future, I will try to make sure those revisions happen much earlier in the process, so that this kind of thing can be avoided.

As I said in my New Year's post, I'm tentatively planning for a March release for File 04, and I'm still on track for that thankfully!

Until next time!

— LockedOn.

notes.title: Devlog 53: Out of the Woods
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/14e1862def0cfb8c236750d3c708f140965c3076.png[/img]

File 04's backgrounds have now been modeled!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/763b5bdf5d8f27c1c8f8a6627826bb3bf8b838cc.png[/img]

Here's what I worked on since the last devlog:

[list]
[*] Backgrounds for File 04
[/list]

To celebrate this milestone, I'm happy to reveal the first official image from File 04:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/f3acc0f50dbfe42841b89cd81bee88a5ce3f38ac.png[/img]

I actually finished these backgrounds a bit ahead of what I estimated — one of the first times I've overestimated how long something will take! Like I explained last time, I first blocked out all of the backgrounds very roughly — basic cubes, and just some simple walls for buildings. This gave me a starting point for all seven backgrounds. Then I did a detail pass where I added textures, lighting, modeled props and got them to look a bit better. Then I did a "mystery props" pass where I modeled and placed all the specific evidence that was needed for the mystery. Finally, a "dummies" pass where I created and placed all the suspect/victim dummies. By that point, all seven backgrounds were finished.

This is in contrast to my approach with the first two Files — completing entire backgrounds one at a time. I believe this made the process go faster, mostly due to psychological reasons — if you only need to complete 20% of a task, suddenly it seems easier. By breaking up the seven backgrounds into "20% tasks", it lowered the psychological barrier for each background.

But there's another reason this worked, which is that File 04 does not have "one big background" — such as the Grouse Mountain Entrance from File 01, the Ubihard Main Office from File 02, or the Museum from File 03. Those big backgrounds were often bottlenecks because it was hard to see the progress being made on them, due to how much more work they required to finish. So in the future, I will take that into consideration and treat those large backgrounds more like separate rooms, or find a way to make them separate rooms.

Now there's just one bunch of assets left for me to finish: the music. So that's what I'll be tackling next!

Until next time!

— LockedOn.

notes.title: Devlog 52: Pieces in Place
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/ae0eea318b789b6d466d80ea34aa4eaf8012673d.png[/img]

File 04 is now roughly blocked out and coded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/a72c72fb8d9e30058a9eb71e5b1ddf65ae4cdc29.png[/img]

Here's what I worked on since the last devlog.

[list]
[*] Rough blocking/coding for File 04
[*] Halloween art
[*] Prison of Lies Enhanced Edition soft launch
[/list]

So, I decided to code File 04 before working on backgrounds/music, as an experiment to see if it would speed up the File's development down the road. What does that actually mean? Here's an exclusive image of File 04 to show you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/b0dcf8bf95b367ac56221f653bb04084e7b60d2f.png[/img]

It means the whole File looks like this right now. I have the characters on screen where they are supposed to appear, they open and close their mouths, but they have no expressions. The puzzles show up but the correct answers are not implemented yet, the methods minigames are not implemented, and there are no CGs or backgrounds. This is why coding is at "90%" complete and not "100%" on the graph. However, even in this primitive state, getting it to this point earlier is going to be really helpful I think. In addition to the benefits I mentioned last time, it also means that towards the end of production on the File, all my focus can be on art assets. What you end up crunching on matters — it's difference between deciding to draw CGs for special moments or to cut them out.

My next task is backgrounds. Because it really helped with File 03, I'm going to be rotating between working on multiple backgrounds at once, instead of getting each one 100% finished one after the other. Just another special trick I'm hoping will speed up the process! ;)

Until next time!

— LockedOn.

notes.title: File 03 is Here!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/2557ac3c75220018ccc84652663349e490c0e82f.jpg[/img]

Note: This update may break old saves as it contains improvements to previous Files!

In this update...

[h1]File 03[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/3b93f8831ede73b34d24494f526b637e3fa8f81b.png[/img]

In the most intriguing mystery yet, Team Tads heads to Iqaluit to investigate a brutal murder in a museum, created by Team Nailbiter. It's the first match-up between Larika and Joane... who will win!?

[b]Please note that the price of the game will increase after this week.[/b]

[h1]Support System[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/0f3be5084ff4740cea160060f017259cc537df24.png[/img]

There is a new gameplay mechanic, "Support", which is very similar to "Theory", however this time you are supporting your teammate's argument with evidence instead of disproving it! There were previously Theory puzzles in File 02 which were solved by supporting statements instead of disproving them, which was inconsistent and therefore confusing — those have now been replaced with Support puzzles. 

[h1]Updated Casefile[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/0db9d60993f589cf8b5539f4c2133b788c058bec.png[/img]

The old casefile tried to cram everything in one screen, and large sections of it were just empty space for most of the mystery. The new casefile is sleeker and tidier, with separate tabs for the case summary, bios of suspects and victims, evidence, and autopsy information. 

You can now click the arrows in the corner of the photo of the crime scene to cycle between various images of the mystery as you discover them.

There's also now a little bio about each suspect and victim to refresh your memory about them, and you can click the dummy icon on their profile picture to see what they look like as dummies, making it easier to identify them.

[h1]Quick-Switching for Morale[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/495d78990e0bfc27e54527474727bc579b9a3ed7.png[/img]

If you're one of the players who likes to unlock the outfits, maybe you've gotten annoyed that in order to unlock those outfits, you may have ended up with certain characters hating you or liking you, and had to replay the Hangout a third time to get them back to where you wanted.

Now once you've unlocked a character's two routes in a Hangout, you can click the "Smile" or "Frown" icons to quickly switch the character to liking you or hating you!

You can also now click the shirt icon to open the Outfits menu and try on their unlocked outfit!

Smaller Improvements!
[list]
[*] CG Gallery added
[*] Interrogation/Theorize layout and text size updated to reduce the need for scrolling on evidence descriptions
[*] Tads' hair is no longer cut off at the top when he is transitioning between standing/sitting poses
[*] Scoring System readjusted
[/list]

Enjoy File 03, and I hope you look forward to the release of Hangout Three... ;)

Best,

— LockedOn & Erabit

I've started to think of my writing process like ice climbing. I vaguely know that my goal is to reach the top, and some key landmarks along the way, but generally I am choosing where to stick my axe and place my feet as I go. It can feel unsafe, and slow, and sometimes painful, but as long as I have confidence and persist with it, I can make it. Does that metaphor make sense?

Thankfully, despite how long it's taking to write, this File is a lot easier to write than File 02. My hope is I can push through and finish the next two chapters by the end of this month, and then it'll be on to the fun part.

Until next time!

notes.title: Devlog 35: Contrast
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/9f475c587a36672c346b878d165ba7c2bc556fa1.png[/img]

Writing continues on File 03...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/a294db283a2eb218c2532c5314409d52de13aa02.png[/img]

Chapter 11 has now been written! I did get a bit stuck writing this chapter, certain scenes weren't quite working. One of my theories about writing is that it's good to focus on contrast rather than conflict. Only focusing on conflict can make characters come off as always argumentative, unlikable, and aggressive. Contrast can bring out conflict, but sometimes all you need in a scene is, for example, two characters who approach things in different ways solving a problem together.

Once I went through with some revisions, I think I was able to clarify the contrasts and the scenes started to work better, and before I knew it, the chapter was written! Going to start plotting out the mystery this week so that I have more of an outline to work with than usual.

Until next time!

— LockedOn

notes.title: File 02 is Here! 🤩
notes.content:
File 02 has been released into Early Access, and the price will increase on Oct 6th, so you will be able to get File 02 at the current price for this week! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/4b7aff43c12db5d7ca805c5db010c38b05d4a063.jpg[/img]

It took a long time, but File 02 has been written, modeled, composed, designed, implemented, tested, and translated — and now is finally in Early Access!

Please note that this update may break your saves, because I've added new systems to File 01.

Speaking of that, this update to the game comes with a few new features and improvements, not just in File 02, but File 01 as well!

[h1]💥Outfits[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/9fe13d0c14b399f154752c42280f99aa935bd5fb.png[/img]

As a reward for completing Hangouts, you now unlock outfits for Team Tads. Hangout One's outfit set, "Casual", is now included! More outfit sets will be released with later Hangouts.

[h1]💥Hangouts[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/35a95598dcb0650269fccec9605fe519445b74bd.png[/img]

The Hangouts now get a special menu where you can see which routes you've unlocked, and navigate to the different Hangouts in the future.

[h1]💥Scoring System[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/160d6fba15aa1ce04006175ef7bdd7775a5934fe.png[/img]

Both File 01 and File 02 have a new scoring system with rank "S" as the highest and "F" as the lowest. See how you score!

[h1]💥Hearts System[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/409983ce2c83bf5bdf26088c5f916b585137da5d.png[/img]

I've implemented a hearts system to the Interrogation and Theorize puzzles. Every incorrect answer loses a heart. If you run out of hearts, you get the chance to "Auto-fill" the correct answer.

[h1]💥Viu Minigame Updates[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/11bb208b43de085bb2f0de2f5cd32c7b11bae2c6.png[/img]

I've implemented feedback from players about Viu's minigame. Now areas "focus" to highlight where you can find eyes. It makes the minigame a lot easier, especially for people who for some reason play the game with a trackpad instead of a mouse (kudos to you for dealing with that), and hopefully encourages more careful searching as opposed to randomly roaming your mouse around.

[h1]💥Music Room[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/6b6754ea7b1d8d859ae69d46efa3edf0611446f7.png[/img]

The music room is here! Listen to the soundtrack in-game, now with functionality to scrub through the track or pause it.*

[h1]💥Achievements[/h1]
Achievements have now been added to the game!

[h1]Smaller Improvements!🙊🙊[/h1]

[list]
[*] The evidence the dummy is being asked about now appears on screen
[*] "Correct!" sound effect for when you submit the right evidence in Interrogations, select the right toxins in Anadyne's minigame, and as positive feedback for positive answers in Hangouts.
[*] Dummy icon now marks dummy interrogations 
[*] Dummies will now be "locked" until you have found the evidence you need for their interrogation, so that you waste less time backtracking
[*] Added casefile summaries
[*] The amount of evidence you need to select for an Interrogation/Theorize puzzle is now simply a UI element, instead of the characters awkwardly discussing it in the hint.
[*] In Chapter 4, Larika will now only say she "almost submitted the wrong answer" if the player did in fact choose to submit the incorrect answer.
[*] Fixed Anadyne's bio.
[/list]

Thanks for supporting the Early Access! With your feedback, I've been able to make improvements to the game.

Enjoy File 02, and see you soon for the release of Hangout Two... ;)

Best,

— LockedOn.

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/5b1d8e077506877176ce3fd6f217cdd8951bb3bb.png[/img]

[i]File 02: Montréal[/i]'s beta launches next Tuesday.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/fe55cd87272d080f706353dbbb43997bcfae8cea.png[/img]

You may be a little surprised because in my last devlog I said that I'd just completed Chapter 7 — after many months of production. Now only eleven days later, the final three chapters are completely finished and beta is set for next Tuesday. So what happened??

Basically, a bit after I began working on File 01, I got a part time job. This is a necessity at the moment — I do not make enough from just game dev to completely cover my monthly expenses. Though it's only part time, I find that it kind of exhausts me, and my productivity levels have definitely been affected. But I've gotten a break for the past two weeks, so I thought I'd make every second count, and spent every waking moment working on File 02 trying to finish it before my break ended — and I managed to do it!


What really kicked it off was trying to create simple, rough versions of all seven remaining backgrounds in just one day. Turns out all I needed was to get the ball rolling, and I basically finished them in only three days. It took a day to complete the remaining sprites. Another to complete the music. The next six days were just implementing code and the minigames.

Even though I worked harder than I've ever worked, staying up way past midnight every day working on it, I was having fun. Something I would like to say about crunch before the File is released is that when you are "crunching" on a personal project, with your characters, your story, about what you are passionate about, and nobody forcing you to do it — I find that a euphoric and exhilarating experience. Every day I felt productive and full of energy, as I could see how fast I was making progress compared to these past few months. "Crunching" on a project for some company that's forcing you to do it is a completely different experience — a horrible one that I wouldn't wish on anybody.

Hopefully File 02 will be ready to launch in early access next month. But if you are impatient, the public beta launches on the 22nd for Patreon and Afdian members. If you are planning to get the game, now is a good time because the price will increase with File 02's release.

notes.title: Devlog 26: Scoring System
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/8b925d6b9e8883d624383d3384a0f58249990a2d.png[/img]

The latest French Canadian devlog...!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/003d3145f5dced967b6990dc868eecad0a5e5f62.png[/img]

The past two weeks I worked on the Outfits system, [url=https://www.lockedongames.com/post/lockedon-12-year-anniversary]which I announced earlier this week for the 12 Year Anniversary of LockedOn Games[/url]. I made a new background, and implemented all dialogue and expression changes along with it. But I was also working through my backlog of player-requested features, which will be retroactively added to File 01.

The mystery-solving sections will now have a scoring system, which will give you a final score based on the number of wrong answers across the entire mystery. "Confrontations" measure the amount of wrong answers during dummy interrogations, "Refutations" for during the Theorize sections, and "Deductions" during the final deduction section.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/d9659d579045c00048266a87b3e6f88c8492535b.png[/img]

You'll notice the "Skipped Theories" counter as well. I've also added a hearts system — for each wrong answer, you lose a "heart". When all the hearts run out, you will be given the option to skip the Theory by auto-filling the correct answer if you are really truly stuck. Of course, this will impact your final rank, but it should be a relief for players who simply want to experience the story but are bogged down with a tricky or obscure puzzle.

Though I had my doubts about it at first, after implementing the scoring and hearts systems, I think they make the gameplay more fun and alleviate some frustrations.

That's not all of the changes coming with the release of File 02, but I hope you enjoyed this first look.

Until next time!

I don't know when all of that will be ready, but my plan is to keep developing the game as it is being translated, so the next file will be able to come out sooner.

In the meantime, enjoy the beta and getting a first look at the game!

Until next time!

— LockedOn.

notes.title: Devlog 15: Breaktime is Over!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/c3c2aeec9c27a482165990742cdc98070da2fc58.png[/img]

My break is over, and I've returned to Canada...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/4c1030affb11968f249c844d83f9b469f7aff99b.png[/img]

This past week I completed a lot of music tracks, and the music for File One is now 77% complete. I have also finished the most difficult part of Chapter 2 — the large number of unique methods minigames.

Chapter 2 has been the main reason File One has taken over fifteen weeks of work. It has the most difficult background to create, the most new UI elements I've ever had to create for one single chapter, as well as the most complex coding.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/487084831b26e1a1c610829fb214d589e9446ec2.png[/img]

[i]A screenshot from Chapter 2[/i]

I was really stuck on these methods minigames — Struess's in particular. How do you make hacking into a simple minigame? There are a lot of different answers, and I looked at my favorite hacking minigames from other games such as Deus Ex Machina: Human Revolution. However, Methods minigames are not as involved as that, and the idea of coding something similar was so daunting that I just felt it was best to keep things as simple as possible.

The methods minigames in File One are about as simple as the ones in Methods — as I make more files there's an opportunity to make them gradually get more complex. 

But with that out of the way, I'm very hopeful about meeting my two week deadline for the beta. File One has been a much greater struggle than I ever anticipated, so I'll be very glad to finish it.

Until next time!

— LockedOn.

notes.title: Devlog 13: Hourly Goals
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/16f729a024fd9a69c7b8031009ef579eb6a3742a.png[/img]

A brand new devlog from Canada! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43128595/e5cb765228253799e0aff6e29c59438f90f7efb0.png[/img]

Last week I began breaking up working sessions into hourly goals that I needed to hit. Creating a sense of urgency really helped me get started, and with this technique, I was able to finish a lot of UI that I may not have otherwise gotten done within the week.

I'm really hoping to finish everything in Chapter 2 by next week. Currently the biggest challenges I have to completing it are needing to create three more new minigames, and making the casefile. 

I will also be taking some breaks over the winter holidays, so my devlogs will briefly become a little more irregular. However it will be back to weekly posts on Tuesdays by January.

Until next time!
